markdown_report:
**Evidence and insights.** The starting recent-mean residual offers a cheap path for current interests. Its scalar gate cannot adapt to changes within a dataset. Electronics misranks 21.89% of sampled fitted pairs. Its recent-deletion HR@10 change is zero, motivating stronger discrimination and a direct recent-history path without establishing their cause. Movies loses 0.155 fitted HR@10 after recent deletion. Preserve its useful sequential encoder rather than replacing it globally.

Three literature insights guide extensions. [Negative-sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) shows that sampler choice changes accuracy and popularity behavior. Popularity sampling therefore needs controls. [MQSA-TED](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056) combines temporal queries with transition information. This motivates asymmetric recent-item scoring, although transitions do not establish complementarity. [MoS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20858) separates temporal interests. A small adaptive gate offers a cheaper hypothesis for this early, 10%-progress stage.

**Framework and candidates.** Organize methods along three axes: discrimination objective, directional representation, and temporal routing. SASRec supplies sequence modeling; the starting idea adds fixed temporal pooling; the selected extension makes that pooling directional and adaptive.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| A: Uniform 32-negative candidate CE | 2/7/4/8/3 | Simple discrimination control; current intent remains implicit. |
| B: Adaptive directional recent residual + A | 5/8/8/8/5 | Direct recent transition path; sparse transitions may generalize poorly. |
| C: Add randomly initialized title-token features to B | 5/7/8/6/7 | Shares evidence across sparse items; lexical similarity can repeat broad associations. |

**Selected: B.** Replace the scalar recent-mean residual with a gate conditioned on the current causal SASRec feature, recent summary, and prefix length. Average the last three nonpadding item embeddings, project this summary through a source matrix, and score candidates through a separate target matrix. Add this gated directional score to SASRec’s score.

This explicitly targets two observed user failures: stale history dominating immediate preferences, and broad similarity outranking a specific recent connection. Directionality models observed follow-on choices rather than symmetric resemblance; it cannot certify compatibility or prevent duplicate capability. Candidate CE targets Electronics’ weak fitted separation.

```python
h = sasrec(sequence)                    # causal features
r = causal_recent_mean(item_emb(sequence), window=3)
g = sigmoid(gate(concat(h, r, log1p(prefix_length))))
score = dot(h, item_emb(candidates)) + g * dot(source(r), target(candidates))
loss = cross_entropy(score, positive_index=0)  # positive + 32 uniform negatives
```

Exclude padding and known training positives from negatives. Use baseline, A, directional-residual-only, and B controls, retaining all four routes and prescribed seeds. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10 within the shared budget. Save both projections and gate; update the predictor writer and diagnostic scoring consistently. Preserve diagnostic interfaces and definitions, treating fitted probes separately from validation. No improvement is measured.

idea.description: Add an adaptive directional recent-history score residual to each per-dataset SASRec and train with uniform 32-negative candidate-set cross-entropy. Preserve SASRec’s sequential score and learn when a recent transition score should contribute.
idea.motivation: Explicitly address stale historical influence and broad similarity displacing specific recent interests. Address the model-facing Electronics failure of weak fitted positive–negative separation, while recognizing that its history insensitivity does not establish a popularity shortcut.
idea.implementation_notes: Use a causal three-event nonpadding mean at every supervised position. Apply separate bias-free source and target projections, and a small sigmoid gate conditioned on SASRec features, recent summary, and log prefix length. Initialize the residual gate conservatively, for example with bias -2. Sample 32 unique uniform negatives per position where the catalog permits, excluding padding, the positive, and known training positives; use the available eligible catalog if smaller. This is candidate-set CE, not a claim of unbiased full-softmax estimation. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, SASREC_EPOCHS default 200, single-GPU execution, all four dataset routes, and trial-local artifacts. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the projections, gate, and identical scoring equation. Keep view.model as the actual module and route view.predict_score through the complete score; adapt feature packing if required. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and their definitions. A scalar fitted_recent_gate becomes null when no scalar parameter exists; report measured adaptive-gate summaries separately. Do not use unavailable review or product attributes. User alignment: 8/10, positive—explicit recent and directional paths target two stated failures; negative—ordered interactions cannot establish immediate intent, compatibility, or ownership needs. Model alignment: 8/10, positive—multi-negative competition directly targets fitted pair misranking; negative—better fitted separation need not improve held-out HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
For each prescribed dataset route:
  Initialize SASRec, source/target projections, and adaptive gate with seed 42.
  For each existing training batch:
    h = causal SASRec features(sequence)
    r = causal mean of up to three most recent nonpadding item embeddings
    g = sigmoid(MLP(concat(h, r, log1p(prefix_length))))
    candidates = positive plus up to 32 eligible unique uniform negatives
    logits = dot(h, item_emb(candidates)) + g * dot(source(r), target(candidates))
    Optimize candidate cross-entropy over valid positive positions.
  Save architecture configuration and complete state beneath the trial directory.
Generate working/predict.py with identical scoring and dataset routing.
Compare baseline, CE-only, residual-only, and combined variants using host macro validation HR@10.
Run compatible training-only diagnostics without presenting them as held-out results.

originality.positive: Combines adaptive recent-history routing with asymmetric transition scoring in a small extension of the supplied scalar residual.
originality.negative: Temporal gates, directional transitions, and candidate cross-entropy are established components; novelty lies in the constrained combination.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact foundation for later timestamp-conditioned routing or public-text parameter sharing, with clear component controls.
future_potential.negative: Sparse directional transitions and limited validation users may make apparent gains unstable.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only causal pooling, two projections, a small gate, and a vectorized candidate loss.
code_difficulty.negative: Training, predictor generation, and diagnostic feature/scoring compatibility must change together; multi-negative tensors add memory cost.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequential encoder retained by the proposed method.
limitations: Learned item IDs alone do not establish product compatibility or represent unseen items reliably.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study supplied in the search results
contributions: Compares sampling strategies and motivates separating objective changes from architecture changes.
limitations: Reported accuracy and popularity tradeoffs do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluator.

related_work.title: MQSA-TED
contributions: Combines temporal attention queries with global transition information, motivating a directional recent-history branch.
limitations: Transition evidence can be weak under sparsity and does not label complementarity or substitution.

related_work.title: MoS
contributions: Uses multiple interest views and routing to address shifting and recurring interests.
limitations: Its full expert architecture exceeds the selected minimal extension, and benchmark transfer remains unmeasured.
